correctness.rationale: Explicit random sign-symmetric 2x2 update matrices yield a closed nonnegative second-moment recursion. Perron theory proves the exact same asymptotic rate for every nonzero start; exact norm decrease/growth proves the iff ω interval. A rank-one secular equation and strictly decreasing S-zS′ produce the unique minimizer. An exact eigenvalue derivative establishes strictly optimal overrelaxation, and critical-root asymptotics produce the factor-two nearly-parallel improvement. The included verifier passed symbolic identities and 6,240 rational cases; the proof, not tests, covers all angles and times.

originality.rationale: Novelty is claimed solely for the exact angle-parametrized rate-minimizing constant relaxation and the factor-two near-parallel improvement, not randomized Kaczmarz, covariance lifting, or general convergence. Full primary-text comparisons find different objectives and updates in classic RK, accelerated RK, exact-MSE inconsistent RK, and scheduled noisy RK. Published-result searches and comparisons with scientific claims show no stronger covered statement. The inaccessible 2012 relaxation chapter and 2014 exact-MSE sampling conference article create named residual originality risks.
residual_risks: An older Kaczmarz relaxation paper (Cai–Zhao–Tang, 2012) was available only through abstract/index, so a special angle-dependent mean-square optimizer cannot be definitively excluded.
The 2014 Agaskar–Wang–Lu exact-MSE/optimal-sampling conference article could not be read fully; it may include algebraic reductions relevant to the present result.

Other stochastic linear-system and projection-method literature could contain equivalent two-line formulations under different terminology. Search absence is not an independence or novelty certificate.

value.rationale: Relaxation-parameter tuning for a universally natural two-equation row-action method is motivated by actual asymptotic convergence speed, and its exact all-angle optimizer avoids ad hoc grid search. The unexpected strict benefit of overrelaxation in every nonorthogonal geometry, and nearly-parallel factor-two spectral-gap improvement, are substantive structural benchmark facts rather than a routine parameter substitution or tiny isolated numerical gain.
